title: Performance tests
description:
This should support running a matrix of archives × ec2 instance types on
any particular point in the git history. Results are saved to a results
bucket. This should allow for performance comparisons relaese to
release.

A script is also provided to create test fixtures in S3, though this only needs to be run once and that has been completed.

title: Do not write zip data descriptor for empty files
description:
Zip [data descriptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_(file_format)#Data_descriptor) are only useful when the file
length and checksum isn't known at LFH write time. For the case of empty
files, we do know those things, so we do not need to write a data
descriptor.

Also simplifies burst_writer_add_file function signature to remove a
redundant parameter specifying the LFH is for an empty file; we can
infer this by looking at the LFH that was passed in.

A Claude analysis reported no impacts to the downloader or to alignment
rule violations as a result of this change.

title: fix: correct ZIP64 data descriptor format detection
description:
The uses_zip64_descriptor field was incorrectly set to true whenever a ZIP64 extra field was present. However, a ZIP64 extra field may exist only for the local_header_offset (when offset > 4GB), while file sizes still fit in 32 bits. The data descriptor format depends on whether SIZES overflow 32-bit, not whether the offset does.

When uses_zip64_descriptor was incorrectly true, the stream processor consumed 24 bytes for the data descriptor instead of 16, causing it to misalign and fail to parse subsequent frames with errors like: "Stream processor error: Failed to parse frame at offset 97132"

The fix checks if compressed_size or uncompressed_size equals 0xFFFFFFFF in the central directory header (indicating the actual values are in the ZIP64 extra field) rather than just checking for ZIP64 extra field presence.

Fixes #9

title: Add GitHub Actions release workflow for Linux binaries
description:
- Build for x86_64 and arm64 on version tags (v*)
- Package binaries with README and LICENSE in tar.gz archives
- Generate SHA256 checksums for each archive
- Auto-publish to GitHub Releases
- Add release process documentation

Also:
- fix README prerequisites: ruby must be installed before cmake for CMock mock generation at build time.
- fix GitHub badge URL to point to posit-dev/burst

Fixes #7

title: Update pinned dependencies, GitHub Actions, and test frameworks
description:
The repo hadn't been touched since March. This updates dependencies that had drifted, and fixes a CI download that now 404s.

## Changes

One commit per change, so a CI failure points at one of them.

- **Pin the AWS CRT libraries to release tags.** All nine were built from `GIT_TAG main`, so each build used whatever upstream had merged that day. They're now pinned to the tags aws-crt-cpp v0.44.5 ships together as submodules. That's the set AWS tests against each other. Each library's newest tag on its own isn't guaranteed to work with the others; s2n-tls is at v1.7.13 rather than its latest v1.7.14 for this reason.
- **Update the GitHub Actions.** `checkout` v2/v4 → v7, `upload-artifact` v4 → v7, `download-artifact` v4 → v8, `configure-aws-credentials` v4 → v6, `action-gh-release` v2 → v3. These majors mostly move to Node 24. The other breaking changes don't apply here: download-artifact's path change only affects downloads by artifact ID (we download by name), and v8 now fails on a digest mismatch, which is the behaviour we want.
- **Update CMock to v2.7.0 and Unity to v2.7.0.** The vendored Unity exactly matched upstream commit `747c2ee`, between v2.6.1 and v2.7.0, so this is a straight copy of v2.7.0's `src/` files. CMock 2.7 compares `void*` arguments by pointer when the array plugin is off, which is how our mocks are configured.
- **Download 7-Zip from its GitHub releases.** `www.7-zip.org/a/7z2408-linux-x64.tar.xz` now returns 404, which would fail the 7-Zip install step in every test job. 7-zip.org links its downloads to `github.com/ip7z/7zip/releases`, so CI fetches 26.06 from there and checks the sha256 GitHub publishes for the file.
- **Bring CLAUDE.md's test list up to date.** It now lists all 13 unit tests and all 4 mock headers, and the test counts per label match what ctest reports.

## Testing

Built on Ubuntu 24.04 in Docker (arm64; CI runs x64):

- All three binaries build with the pinned AWS libraries.
- All 14 non-integration tests pass, with mocks regenerated by CMock 2.7.
- All 7 integration tests that don't need S3, BTRFS or sudo pass with 7-Zip 26.06.

Not run locally: the S3, BTRFS and end-to-end tests. This PR's CI run is their first run with these changes.

## Notes

- An existing local `build/` keeps its old CMock 2.5.3 mocks, because the mock build rule depends on the mock headers and config but not on the CMock version. Delete `build/tests/mocks` to regenerate them. CI always builds from scratch, so it isn't affected.
- A roborev review of the branch flagged three issues in Unity 2.7.0 itself: `NOT_EQUAL_STRING_LEN`, `EACH_EQUAL_MEMORY` and the float failure message. Our tests use none of those assertions, and `tests/unity/` is left as an exact copy of upstream.

title: Preserve setuid bits, capabilities, xattrs and mtimes on restore
description:
Fixes #14
Fixes #15
Fixes #16

- The downloader sets the owner before the mode, so chown no longer clears setuid, setgid or file capabilities.
- The writer records mtimes in the Info-ZIP extended timestamp field (0x5455), only for entries that have one, and xattrs in a new central-directory field (0x4258, described in `docs/burst-format.md`).
- The downloader applies xattrs and mtimes after all parts finish, since a later write to a file that spans parts would clear its capabilities and move its mtime.

`test_e2e_unix_metadata` now covers setuid, capabilities, `user.*` xattrs and mtimes. New unit test `test_timestamp_field_only_with_recorded_mtime`.

title: Rename continuing_file to last_file_before_part
description:
Follow-up to the part-boundary restore fix. After that change, the part map no longer decides whether a file continues into a part. It records the last file starting before each part, and the part's first frame decides:

- a Start-of-Part frame means that file continues here
- a local header or the central directory means it ended in an earlier part

The old names implied the part map had already made that decision, so this renames:

- `part_files.continuing_file` → `last_file_before_part`
- `STATE_CONTINUING_FILE` → `STATE_CHECK_PART_START`

Comments that described the field as definitely continuing are reworded to match. Nothing else changes.

Test function names such as `test_continuing_file_detection` are unchanged, since they describe the behaviour under test rather than the field.

## Testing

`make test-unit`: 14/14 passed.

title: Fix restores of parts that start with a data descriptor
description:
Fixes #17

- Writer: the recorded compressed size now includes the padding and Start-of-Part frames written inside a file's data.
- Downloader: the file that continues into a part is the last file starting before it. If that file ended before the part, the part starting with a local header or the central directory is accepted. Parts that start inside the central directory get no continuing file.

Archives from v0.0.3 restore with the fixed downloader. New unit tests in `test_central_dir_parser` and `test_stream_processor`, and a new end-to-end test, `test_e2e_descriptor_boundary`.

title: Add an S3 endpoint option to burst-downloader
description:
Adds `--endpoint` to `burst-downloader` for S3-compatible services such as localstack. The end-to-end tests and `setup_s3.sh` use it when `BURST_TEST_ENDPOINT` is set, so they can run without real S3.

Also makes `test_large_cd.sh` fail when the large central directory path isn't exercised; it previously passed either way.

title: Label unit tests so the release workflow runs them
description:
The release workflow runs `ctest -L unit`, but no test had the `unit` label, so the step selected zero tests and passed without running anything.

This labels every test built from `tests/unit/` as `unit`, plus `test_central_dir_parser_integration`, which only reads `tests/fixtures`. `release.yaml` is unchanged.

Checked on Ubuntu 24.04 with the release build flags:
- before: `ctest -N -L unit` lists 0 tests
- after: it lists 14, and `ctest -L unit --output-on-failure` passes 14/14
- `-L unit` selects no `integration`, `s3`, `btrfs`, `e2e` or `slow` test
- the 14 are the same tests `test.yaml` runs with `make test-unit` (`ctest -LE integration`)

title: Build x86_64 releases on Ubuntu 24.04
description:
Fixes #18

`ubuntu-latest` is now Ubuntu 26.04, so x86_64 release binaries need OpenSSL 3.4 and won't start on 24.04. This pins the x86_64 release runner to `ubuntu-24.04`, matching the arm64 build's `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.

title: Mount the e2e BTRFS filesystem under tests/tmp
description:
`tests/integration/e2e/setup_btrfs.sh` is three directories below the repo root but went up two, so the loop image and BTRFS mount landed in `tests/tests/tmp/` instead of `tests/tmp/`. That path isn't gitignored, and the script's unmount note and "pre-create BTRFS mount at" hint pointed at `tests/tmp/btrfs`, where nothing was.

The e2e tests only use the exported `$BTRFS_MOUNT_DIR`, so they need no changes.

Checked by sourcing the script in a privileged container:
- before: mounts at `tests/tests/tmp/btrfs` and creates `tests/tests/`
- after: mounts at `tests/tmp/btrfs` (btrfs), no `tests/tests/`

Machines with an existing mount at `tests/tests/tmp/btrfs` will get a new one at `tests/tmp/btrfs` on the next run; the old one can be removed with `sudo umount tests/tests/tmp/btrfs` and `sudo losetup -d`.
